# MLM Initial Interaction

## Affect Valence
```{r}
contrasts(MegaAnalysisMaster$ParadigmsCombined_Factor) = contr.sum(6)

InitialModel_MLM_EmoValence <- lme(Emotional_Valance_Std ~ 1 + + Has_Phone*Gender + Has_Phone* ParadigmsCombined_Factor  + Age + Gender ,   #Fixed effects portion of model
                        data = MegaAnalysisMaster, #Which data to use
                        random = ~  Has_Phone | ParadigmsCombined_Factor, #Random effects portion of model
                        method="ML", #Estimation method
                        na.action="na.omit") #missing data handling
summary(InitialModel_MLM_EmoValence)
```


```{r}
tab_model(InitialModel_MLM_EmoValence, digits = 3, digits.re = 5)
```


## Social Connectedness
```{r}
contrasts(MegaAnalysisMaster$ParadigmsCombined_Factor) = contr.sum(6)
InitialModel_MLM_SocialConnection <- lme(SocialConnection_Std~ 1 + Has_Phone * Gender + Has_Phone*ParadigmsCombined_Factor + Gender + Age + Gender ,   #Fixed effects portion of model
                        data = MegaAnalysisMaster, #Which data to use
                        random = ~  Has_Phone | ParadigmsCombined_Factor, #Random effects portion of model
                        method="ML", #Estimation method
                        na.action="na.omit") #missing data handling
summary(InitialModel_MLM_SocialConnection)
```

## Social Connectedness Predicting Mood

### Main Effects 


```{r}

TechDirect.SocConnect_Mood.1.5 <-

```

```{r}
anova(TechDirect.SocConnect_Mood.1, TechDirect.SocConnect_Mood.2, TechDirect.SocConnect_Mood.3)
```

```{r}
TechDirect.SocConnect_Mood_SimpEff
```

```{r}
pairs(TechDirect.SocConnect_Mood_SimpEff)
```
```{r}

SocConnect_EmmeansData$interval <- SocConnect_EmmeansData$SE * 1.96

ggplot(SocConnect_EmmeansData, aes(x=Has_Phone, y=yvar, fill=Has_Phone)) +
  facet_wrap(~Gender) + 
  geom_point(position=position_dodge(), stat="identity",

```

```{r}
ggsave('Mood - EMMeans - Controlling For Social Connectedness - Tech Directions.png', width = 6, height = 6)
```

## Difficulty Finding Building

One idea for the disparity between Tech directions Gender effect and the other studies Gender effect is that men and women may have different levels of difficulty finding the builiding which lead women to benefit more from using their phone than men. So I am running 2 types of models

1.Gender and Condition predicting Difficulty of finding building
2.Gender, Condition, and Difficulty of finding building predicting Mood

### Reverse Coding
```{r}
TechDirections_Tight$Ease_locating.building <- ((TechDirections_Tight$Difficulty_locating.building - 7) * -1)

describe(TechDirections_Tight$Difficulty_locating.building)

describe(TechDirections_Tight$Ease_locating.building)
```


### Gender and Condtion predicting Difficulty

#### Main Effects

We find a main effect of phone, with those with their phone report a reduction in difficulty in finding the buildings. This at least is a good indicator that complimentarity is happened.
There is no gender main effect.
```{r}

TechDirect.FindingBuilding.1 <-
        lm(Ease_locating.building ~ Has_Phone + Gender,
           TechDirections_Tight)

summary(TechDirect.FindingBuilding.1)

```


#### Interactions
In running the interaction, we find no interaction between Gender and Phones. So Men and Women seem to have the same effect 
```{r}

TechDirect.FindingBuilding.2 <-
        lm(Ease_locating.building~ Has_Phone * Gender,
           TechDirections_Tight)

summary(TechDirect.FindingBuilding.2)

```
```{r}
anova(TechDirect.FindingBuilding.1, TechDirect.FindingBuilding.2)
```

#### Simple Effects

This is the simple effects of phone when seperating by gender.
```{r}

TechDirect.FindingBuilidng_SimpEff <- emmeans(TechDirect.FindingBuilding.2, 'Has_Phone', by = 'Gender') 
TechDirect.FindingBuilidng_SimpEff

contrast(TechDirect.FindingBuilidng_SimpEff)
```
```{r}
pairs(TechDirect.FindingBuilidng_SimpEff)
```

##### Graph
```{r}
TechDirections_Tight$Gender <- as.factor(TechDirections_Tight$Gender)
TechDirections_Tight$Has_Phone <- as.factor(TechDirections_Tight$Has_Phone)

TechDirections_Tight$Gender <- recode_factor(TechDirections_Tight$Gender, `0` = "Female", `1` = "Male")
TechDirections_Tight$Has_Phone<- recode_factor(TechDirections_Tight$Has_Phone, `0` = "No Phone", `1` = "Phone")

TechDirections_TightGraphs <- subset(TechDirections_Tight, Gender == "Female" | Gender == "Male")

TechDirections_TightGraphs <- subset(TechDirections_TightGraphs, Has_Phone == "No Phone"|  Has_Phone == "Phone")
```


```{r}


ggplot(TechDirections_TightGraphs, aes(x=Has_Phone, y=Difficulty_locating.building, fill=Has_Phone, col=Has_Phone, na.rm=TRUE)) +
    geom_flat_violin(position = position_nudge(x = .2, y = 0), alpha = .2, adjust = 4)+
    geom_point(position=position_jitter(width = .15),size = 1, alpha = 1/3)+
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("#F26627", "#325D79"))+
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("#F26627", "#325D79"))+
    guides(fill = FALSE, col = FALSE, )+ 
  facet_wrap(~Gender) + 
  geom_boxplot(aes(x = as.numeric(Has_Phone)+ 0.25, y = Difficulty_locating.building),outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.4, width = .1, colour = "BLACK") + 
 stat_summary(fun.data = "mean_cl_normal", geom = "errorbar", width = 1/4, color = "black") + 
 stat_summary(fun = "mean", geom = "point", shape = 23, stroke = 1, size = 1.5,  color = "black", fill = "gold") +
  ylab('Ratings of Diffulty of Finding The Building')+ 
  xlab('Condition') + 
  theme_apa() + 
  scale_y_continuous(breaks=seq(0,7,1))
```




```{r}
ggsave('Difficulty Finding Building by Phone & Gender - Tech Directions.png', width = 6, height = 6) 
```

## Number Of Social Interactions
Social.Interactions_#

### Gender and Condtion predicting Difficulty

#### Main Effects

We find a main effect of phone, with those with their phone reporting less social interactions. This at least is a good indicator that displacement is happened.
There is no gender main effect.
```{r}

TechDirect.SocialInteraction.1 <-
        lm(`Social.Interactions_#` ~ Has_Phone + Gender,
           TechDirections_Tight)

summary(TechDirect.SocialInteraction.1)

```


#### Interactions

In running the interaction, we find no interaction between Gender and Phones. So Men and Women seem to have the same effect 
```{r}

TechDirect.SocialInteraction.2 <-
        lm(`Social.Interactions_#` ~ Has_Phone * Gender,
           TechDirections_Tight)

summary(TechDirect.SocialInteraction.2)

```

```{r}
anova(TechDirect.SocialInteraction.1, TechDirect.SocialInteraction.2)
```

#### Simple Effects

This is the simple effects of phone when seperating by gender.
```{r}

TechDirect.SocialInteraction_SimpEff <- emmeans(TechDirect.SocialInteraction.2, 'Has_Phone', by = 'Gender') 
TechDirect.SocialInteraction_SimpEff

contrast(TechDirect.SocialInteraction_SimpEff)
```

```{r}
pairs(TechDirect.SocialInteraction_SimpEff)
```


### Gender, Condition, and # of Social Interactions Predicting Mood

We find a similar outcome to what we had before, though social interaction did not predict emotional valance. One of the key things to note about this analysis is that we lose degrees of freedom because the question about the number of social interactions was not asked during the first experiment. So there is not enough power to find larger effects, which is something to keep in mind. That direcitonality will be the best indicator for the moment.

#### Main Effects 

```{r}

TechDirect.SocialInteraction_Mood.1 <-
        lm(Emotional_Valance_Std ~ Has_Phone +  Gender + SocialConnection_Std +  Difficulty_locating.building +  `Social.Interactions_#` ,
           TechDirections_Tight)

summary(TechDirect.SocialInteraction_Mood.1)

```


#### Interactions

##### Phone Gender Interaction Only
We still get a significant interaction between gender and phone when controlling for number of social interactions.
```{r}

TechDirect.SocialInteraction_Mood.3 <-
        lm(Emotional_Valance_Std ~ Has_Phone * Gender + SocialConnection_Std +  Difficulty_locating.building + `Social.Interactions_#` ,
           TechDirections_Tight)

summary(TechDirect.SocialInteraction_Mood.3)

```

##### Interction All

In this interaction we find that only one is significnant and it's the interaction between having phone and number of social interactions. this may be because of overspecifying this model so for the next step I am going to reduce the interaction only to Phone and Social Interactions to accompany the phone and gender interaction.

```{r}

TechDirect.SocialInteraction_Mood.4 <-
        lm(Emotional_Valance_Std ~ Has_Phone * Gender * `Social.Interactions_#` ,
           TechDirections_Tight)

summary(TechDirect.SocialInteraction_Mood.4)

```

##### Phone x Gender + Phone x Social Interactions
```{r}

TechDirect.SocialInteraction_Mood.5 <-
        lm(Emotional_Valance_Std ~ Has_Phone * Gender + SocialConnection_Std +  Difficulty_locating.building + Has_Phone * `Social.Interactions_#` ,
           TechDirections_Tight)

summary(TechDirect.SocialInteraction_Mood.5)

```

# Full Data

## Phone Use

#### Model X - Predicting Phone Use
```{r}
PhoneUse_lme <- lme(Phone_Use_Frequency_Std ~ 1 + Gender + Age,   #Fixed effects portion of model
                        data = MegaAnalysisMaster, #Which data to use
                        random = ~ 1 | ParadigmsCombined, #Random effects portion of model
                        subset = Has_Phone == "Phone",
                        method="ML", #Estimation method
                        na.action="na.omit") #missing data handling
summary(PhoneUse_lme)
```


#### Model 2 - Phone + Gender + Age + Phone Use
```{r}
PhoneUse_lme.2 <- lme(Emotional_Valance_Std ~ 1 + Gender + Phone_Use_Frequency_Std + Age,   #Fixed effects portion of model
                        data = MegaAnalysisMaster, #Which data to use
                        random = ~  1 | ParadigmsCombined, #Random effects portion of model
                        subset = Has_Phone == "Phone",
                        method="ML", #Estimation method
                        na.action="na.omit") #missing data handling
summary(PhoneUse_lme.2)
```

#### Model 3 - Phone + Gender + Age + Phone Use
```{r}
PhoneUse_lme.3 <- lme(Emotional_Valance_Std ~ 1 + Has_Phone * Gender + Age + Gender * Phone_Use_Frequency_Std,   #Fixed effects portion of model
                        data = MegaAnalysisMaster, #Which data to use
```

# Values for the Forest Plot - Valance Affect
## Effect sizes for each study

This analysis is running OLS regressions on each of the studies to determine individual study effects. The only variables to include are Social Connectedness, Affect Valance, & Condition


#### Getting Directions
```{r}
Forest_GetDirect <- lm(Emotional_Valance_Std ~ Has_Phone, data = MegaAnalysisMaster, subset = ParadigmsCombined == 1 )#& Age != "NA" & Gender != "NA")
  
summary(Forest_GetDirect)


```

```{r}
MegaAnalysisMaster %>%
  filter(ParadigmsCombined == 1) %>%
    cohens_d(Emotional_Valance_Std ~ Has_Phone, data = .) 
```

```{r}
AffectValanceForest <- data.frame(Paradigm=c('Getting Directions', 'Parents with Children', 'Strong Ties Meal', 'Weak Ties Meal', 'Waiting Room Alone', 'Waiting Room Together'),
                       index=1:6,
                       Effect=c(.17898, -.06839, -.14839, -.03218, -.14240, -.18201),
                       Std_Err=c(.11868, .10083, .11458, .12379, .17800, .10371))

AffectValanceForest <- AffectValanceForest %>%
  mutate(
    ConfidenceInt = Std_Err * 1.96,
    LowerInt = Effect - ConfidenceInt,
    UpperInt = Effect + ConfidenceInt
  )


```


```{r}
AffectValanceForestD <- data.frame(Paradigm=c('Getting Directions', 'Parents with Children', 'Strong Ties Meal', 'Weak Ties Meal', 'Waiting Room Alone', 'Waiting Room Together'),
                       index=1:6,
                       Effect=c(.18, -.07, -.15, -.03, -.14, -.18),
                       LowerInt=c(-.05, -.27, -.37, -.27, -.49, -.39),
                       UpperInt=c(.41, .13, .08, .21, .21, .02))
```


## Forest Plot - Affect Valance

```{r}
AffectForectPlot <- ggplot(data=AffectValanceForest, aes(y=index, x=Effect, xmin=LowerInt, xmax=UpperInt, label = Effect)) +
  geom_point() + geom_text (hjust = .5, vjust = -1) +
  geom_errorbarh(height=.1) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks=1:nrow(AffectValanceForest), labels=AffectValanceForest$Paradigm) +
  labs(title='Beta by Study for Affect Valance', x='Beta from Phone Condition', y = 'Study') +
  geom_vline(xintercept=0, color='black', linetype='dashed', alpha=.5) +
  theme_apa()

AffectForectPlot
```


```{r}
AffectForectPlot <- ggplot(data=AffectValanceForestD, aes(y=index, x=Effect, xmin=LowerInt, xmax=UpperInt, label = Effect)) +

  geom_errorbarh(height=.1) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks=1:nrow(AffectValanceForest), labels=AffectValanceForest$Paradigm) +
```

## Getting Numbers for Power Analysis between groups
```{r}
MegaAnalysisMaster %>%
  filter(!is.na(Age) & !is.na(Gender) & !is.na(Has_Phone) & !is.na(ParadigmsCombined) & !is.na(Emotional_Valance_Std)) %>% group_by(ParadigmsCombined) %>% tally()
```

```{r}
MegaAnalysisMaster %>%
  filter(!is.na(Age) & !is.na(Gender) & !is.na(Has_Phone) & !is.na(ParadigmsCombined) & !is.na(Emotional_Valance_Std)) %>%  tally()
```
